newsitem.title: USA: Judge orders release of tapes in ADM civil case.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders release of tapes in ADM civil case.

text.p: A federal judge presiding over civil class action lawsuits against Archer Daniels Midland Co has again ordered the U.S. Justice Department to turn over a portion of the surveillance tapes it gathered in a price-fixing investigation.
Judge Michael Mihm of the U.S. District Court for the Central District of Illinois ruled Thursday that the Justice Department has 14 days to comply with his order.

Access to the tapes is being sought by plaintiffs in class-action suits against ADM and three other defendants, A.E. Staley Manufacturing Co., a unit of Tate & Lyle PLC, Cargill Inc, and American Maize Products Co.
In their suits, plaintiffs claim they were harmed by alleged price fixing in the market for high-fructose corn syrup, a sweetener used in foods and beverages.

Mihm had previously ruled that Justice must share with the plaintiffs portions of the surveillance tapes that had previously been played to a group of ADM directors and those portions of the tapes that deal with lysine, a feed additive.

Last year, ADM pleaded guilty to federal criminal charges of fixing prices of lysine and citric acid, an additive used in foods and other products. The Decatur, Ill.-based agribusiness giant agreed to pay $100 million in fines.
ADM was given immunity from further prosecution under the federal antitrust investigation. It also settled some customer class-action lawsuits involving lysine and citric acid.
The Justice Department has refused to turn over the tapes, contending they contain potential evidence in continuing criminal price-fixing investigations in Atlanta and San Francisco.
